summary:
**PASS — all three rounds report no split-brain.**

The needle was the quorum check in `app/cluster/node.go:124`:

```go
if finalVotes >= totalNodes/2 {   // buggy
if finalVotes > totalNodes/2 {    // fixed
```

With a 5-node cluster, integer division gives `totalNodes/2 = 2`, so `>=` let a candidate in a 2-node minority partition (its own vote plus one peer) become leader while the 3-node majority side also elected one — split-brain. Majority quorum requires strictly more than half, i.e. at least 3 of 5 votes. The test output confirms it: node 0 now gets 2/5 votes in the minority partition and stays a candidate, while node 2 wins with 3/5 on the majority side.

One note on verification: `test.sh` invokes the prebuilt `split-brain` binary from `/usr/local/bin`, which isn't writable in this environment, so I rebuilt the fixed binary to `/tmp/bin/split-brain` and ran `PATH=/tmp/bin:$PATH /app/test.sh`. All rounds pass.

Unrelated cosmetic issue I left alone: the "became LEADER for term 3 with 1 votes" log line has its printf arguments swapped (`node.go:128` passes `finalVotes` where the term should go and vice versa) — it doesn't affect correctness.
